events.factual_description: Park Avenue Armory presents Music for 18 Musicians: Staged Variations in the Wade Thompson Drill Hall from Wednesday, October 14 through Sunday, October 18, 2026. Wednesday through Saturday performances begin at 7:00 PM and Sunday begins at 3:00 PM; the production runs approximately three hours and thirty minutes. The Armory frames the production around both the 50th anniversary of Music for 18 Musicians' premiere and Steve Reich's 90th birthday. Alan Pierson stages and music-directs a cycling durational version that brings together the original Steve Reich Ensemble, Alarm Will Sound and next-generation musicians from Manhattan School of Music, with the musicians encircling the audience and connective interludes by special guest artists. John Heginbotham is credited for movement and associate direction, Urs Schönebaum for lighting design and Mark Grey for sound design. Tickets start at $55 including fees. The current primary page does not name the special guest artists or individual Manhattan School musicians, so none are inferred.

en.why_it_matters: Fifty years after its premiere, Reich's pulse machine is being rebuilt as a three-and-a-half-hour spatial cycle rather than revived as a standard concert piece. The Steve Reich Ensemble, Alarm Will Sound and Manhattan School musicians place three generations inside the same architecture while Alan Pierson turns the Drill Hall itself into part of the score. The anniversary matters because the staging asks what Music for 18 Musicians can become now, not because a round number needs celebrating.
en.trip_verdict: If New York is already in play, actively make room for one of the five performances and let the Armory anchor that part of the trip. From the DMV, I would pair it with another strong New York reason rather than build a dedicated trip around a run that offers several chances to catch the production.

es.why_it_matters: Cincuenta años después del estreno, la máquina de pulsos de Reich se reconstruye como un ciclo espacial de tres horas y media, no como una reposición convencional de concierto. Steve Reich Ensemble, Alarm Will Sound y músicos de Manhattan School ponen tres generaciones dentro de la misma arquitectura, mientras Alan Pierson convierte el Drill Hall en parte de la partitura. El aniversario importa porque el montaje pregunta en qué puede convertirse hoy Music for 18 Musicians, no porque haya que festejar un número redondo.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York ya está en juego, sí haría espacio para una de las cinco funciones y dejaría que el Armory ancle esa parte del viaje. Desde el DMV, la combinaría con otra razón fuerte para subir en vez de armar un viaje dedicado alrededor de una producción que ofrece varias oportunidades para verla.
